text: Risk management is a key part of any successful project. It starts with identifying risks before they become real problems. For example, a team might face risks such as late deliveries, technical failures, or budget cuts. Once these risks are known, the next step is to plan mitigation strategies. This means taking actions to reduce the chance of a risk happening or to lessen its impact. For instance, ordering materials early can prevent delays. However, not every risk can be avoided. That is why contingency plans are also important. These are backup plans, like using a different supplier if the first one fails. Finally, monitoring is essential. By checking risks regularly, you can catch changes early and update your plans. This keeps the project on track and helps the team feel more prepared.
